articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is back. What happens next?
articles.description: After the leather-jacketed CEO, president, and co-founder of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, acknowledged an affair with Megaspeed exec Alice Huang, his company initially announced an investigation. However, after The New York Times reported there was evidence of another affair, this time with an Nvidia executive who reported directly to him, a board meeting that night ended with Huang’s resignation, and Nvidia CFO Colette Kress was installed as the new interim CEO. And then… Huang was back. In recent years, Nvidia has become a key part of the Trump administration’s AI push, a central figure in negotiations over potential Chinese access to cutting-edge AI hardware, and a company that has used its now $4 trillion-plus market cap to finance other AI companies. Saying it received input “from senior levels of the United States government,” Nvidia’s board announced his return as CEO on November 23rd, less than two weeks after his resignation. Nvidia’s Q3 earnings hit the mark, without mentioning the whole Jensen Huang thing The DOJ says it’s investigating Megaspeed Jensen Huang says he’s willing to return as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will testify before lawmakers on December 1st. Oh, so now Nvidia cares about national security and export controls? Tech leaders are convinced that Jensen Huang’s exit was a plot against him Nvidia’s board is reportedly ‘not considering’ hiring Jensen Huang back Trump says it ‘certainly isn’t a bad idea’ for Jensen Huang to return to Nvidia Feds add more rules restricting foreign access to advanced AI chips and servers.
